title: Linux Kernel Developer
summary: Linux kernel developers write and fix code inside the Linux kernel, the core of the operating system, such as device drivers (code that controls hardware) and memory or scheduler changes. They sit in a platform or systems software team and send their changes for public review to the kernel community.
dailyDuties: Write and fix device driver code in C
Debug kernel crashes from logs, traces and crash dumps
Send patch series and answer reviewer comments
Rebase product kernels on new mainline releases
Run driver and stress tests on real hardware

skills.expectation: Work inside Linux kernel subsystems and get patches accepted upstream
Write kernel C that follows the kernel coding style
Write and maintain Linux device drivers
Handle locking, interrupts and concurrency safely
Prepare patch series with git and rebase on mainline
Debug hangs and crashes with JTAG, gdb or crash dumps
Discuss patches in public review with maintainers
Work on KVM or virtio drivers
Understand the network stack for NIC drivers
Drive buses such as I2C and SPI from drivers
Read user-space tools written in C++
